ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording a total wind output of 3.6 GW, with Scottish wind generation estimated at 1.6 GW, operating at only 15.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. While Scotland maintains an exemplary carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, structural transmission bottlenecks prevent this surplus renewable power from displacing thermal generation down south, where the GB-wide carbon intensity sits at 177 gCO2/kWh. As a consequence of these north-to-south export limits, 835 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids. This curtailment has accrued a direct constraint cost of about £46,810. To maintain overall grid balance, system operators were forced to replace this lost clean electricity by burning an estimated 158,555 m3 of fossil gas elsewhere on the network, needlessly adding 292 tonnes of CO2 to the atmosphere. Extrapolating today’s baseline, the estimated total yearly cost of curtailment reaches £17 million. When socialised across national consumption, this inefficiency increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £0.06/MWh, underlining the critical financial and environmental necessity of accelerating cross-border grid infrastructure upgrades to prevent zero-carbon energy from going to waste.
